source_user: A service receives a mix of short prompts and long generations. Design an evaluation plan that reports TTFT, TPOT, throughput, queueing, and P99 latency. Scenario variant 235: include an explicit falsifiable hypothesis and a controlled experiment.
source_assistant: Answer should state assumptions, a falsifiable hypothesis, measurements, expected confounders, and rollback criteria. Minimum technical points: separate prefill and decode behavior; fix workload distribution; report warmup; use repeated trials; capture GPU memory and request-level traces.
corrected_answer:
Scope and assumptions (variant 1235, framing: System Design). Assume one decoder-only LLM served by a continuous-batching engine (vLLM/TensorRT-LLM class) with paged KV cache, a fixed tensor-parallel degree, homogeneous GPUs, and a single model version pinned for the whole study. Traffic is bimodal: short prompts (~128-512 input tokens) paired with long generations (~512-2048 output tokens), interleaved with short-in/short-out requests. Every number below is an estimate to be measured, not a platform fact; if the assumptions break, the plan must be re-derived because prefill/decode ratio drives all five metrics.

Mechanism. TTFT = queue wait + scheduling delay + prefill compute. Prefill is compute-bound and grows roughly with total prefilled tokens (attention adds a superlinear term at long context). TPOT is the steady-state decode step time, dominated by HBM bandwidth for weight and KV reads, so it grows with concurrent batch size and with accumulated KV length. Throughput (output tok/s) rises with batch size until either KV-cache blocks or memory bandwidth saturate; past that knee, added load converts directly into queueing and P99 blowup. These are separate regimes and must never be summarized by a single average latency.

Falsifiable hypothesis (the controlled experiment centers on chunked prefill vs default scheduler). H1: enabling chunked prefill with a token budget of ~2048 tokens per scheduler step reduces decode-phase TPOT p99 by >=20% at 80% of saturation load, while increasing mean TTFT by <=15%. Null: the effect size is within the noise band, defined as the 95% CI half-width of the baseline arm.

Experiment design. Two arms, baseline vs treatment, identical hardware, identical model weights and engine build, only chunked prefill vs default scheduler changed. Use a pre-recorded request trace with fixed seeds and fixed input/output token lengths so realized work is identical across arms; enforce output length with min/max new tokens so the treatment cannot win by generating less. Drive load open-loop with a Poisson arrival process at a staircase of offered rates (e.g. 25/50/75/90/100/110% of the baseline saturation rate) to locate the knee and avoid coordinated omission. Discard a warmup window and demonstrate stationarity before counting samples. Repeat each cell at least 5 times in randomized, interleaved order; report medians with bootstrap CIs, never a single run. Lock GPU clocks or record them, and record power and throttle reasons.

Measurements. Per-request trace with arrival, admission, first-token and last-token timestamps plus input/output token counts, so TTFT can be decomposed into queue wait vs prefill compute, and TPOT computed over the decode phase only. Server-side scheduler counters: batch size distribution, KV block utilization, preemption/recompute counts, prefix cache hit rate. Device telemetry at 1 Hz via DCGM: HBM bandwidth, SM occupancy, power, throttle reasons, memory footprint. For multi-GPU arms also collect NCCL collective time share and topology (nvidia-smi topo -m). Report P50/P90/P99 with sample counts; a P99 from fewer than ~1000 samples per cell is not trustworthy.

Expected confounders. Coordinated omission from closed-loop clients; prefix caching inflating TTFT gains on repetitive synthetic prompts; unequal realized output lengths; cold-start effects (CUDA graph capture, kernel autotuning, page-cache-cold weights); thermal/clock drift over long runs; noisy neighbors and other tenants on the same node; client-side and network latency being attributed to the server; tokenizer differences changing token counts between arms.

Evidence required before believing the result: prefill chunking token budget, plus the per-request trace, the staircase throughput curve with the identified knee, and reproduction on a second independent day.

Rollback criteria and safety. Stage the change in shadow or on a small canary slice first. Roll back immediately if: TPOT p99 regression >25% or TTFT mean regression >15% for two consecutive 10-minute windows; or if error rate, timeout rate, or preemption-induced recompute rises above baseline; or if any correctness check on generated output regresses. Keep the previous engine config and model version hot so rollback is a routing flip, not a redeploy. Do not promote a config whose gain is not reproduced across two independent measurement days.

Reporting discipline. State clearly which numbers are measured on this cluster and which are extrapolations. A serving-performance result is a statement about this hardware, this engine version, and this workload mix only; it is not evidence about model quality or about any other deployment.
